item.text: {"question_id":"4B.1","answer":"During the 2023 election period, Tshisekedi’s administration presided over formal and partly inclusive competition: elections were held on the normal legal schedule; 26 presidential candidacies were validated, including two reinstated by the Constitutional Court; party registration was broad; municipal elections and a diaspora-voting pilot occurred; and citizen observers participated. CENI also commissioned a mixed national-international audit that declared the voter register reliable, although this was an institutional and self-reported CENI assessment rather than direct evidence of presidential independence or genuinely fair implementation. [BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0001-E015, BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0027-E001] The evidence nevertheless does not establish reliably genuine contestability. Observers reported under-registration, delayed or absent polling, nontransparent or disputed register auditing, conflicting voter totals, duplicated polling stations, procedural noncompliance, extended voting, opaque tabulation, alleged voting in military schools, and annulled results. [BATCH-0001-E013, BATCH-0001-E016, BATCH-0007-E010, BATCH-0005-E002, BATCH-0005-E006, BATCH-0013-E008, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0019-E013, BATCH-0028-E011, BATCH-0028-E014] Conflict prevented voting in Rutshuru and Masisi and disenfranchised hundreds of thousands; women were only 12.8% of initially elected National Assembly members, and other groups were significantly underrepresented. [BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E011, BATCH-0001-E015] The campaign was competitive but was marred by violence, including attacks implicating UDPS supporters, unequal administrative resources, and intimidation; the election was subsequently characterized by HRW as highly contested and by CENCO as an electoral catastrophe, though these assessments do not prove Tshisekedi personally directed fraud or violence. [BATCH-0002-E013, BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0028-E014] Tshisekedi was declared the presidential winner and his coalition won 450 of 477 confirmed legislative seats, but opposition candidates and citizens disputed the result, citing extensive irregularities. [BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0013-E008, BATCH-0028-E014] Authorities prohibited an opposition march seeking annulment or a rerun, deployed police to prevent gatherings, and police physically assaulted protesters; allegations that live ammunition was used remained unverified and police gave a conflicting account. [BATCH-0021-E009, BATCH-0010-E022] No verified opposition victory occurred, so acceptance of such a victory was not directly tested. The record supports formal electoral access and some institutional adjudication, but not a finding that Tshisekedi implemented administration making power genuinely contestable. Most operational failures are attributed to CENI, courts, authorities, ruling-party supporters, or conflict conditions rather than personally to Tshisekedi; the supplied evidence does not determine whether irregularities changed the presidential result or establish his personal control over those actors.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0001-E015","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0027-E001","BATCH-0028-E010","BATCH-0001-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E013","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0001-E016","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0007-E010","BATCH-0010-E022","BATCH-0013-E008","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0019-E013","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0028-E011","BATCH-0028-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal direction, knowledge, or control regarding CENI, police, courts, ruling-party supporters, administrative-resource abuse, or local violence.","The constitutional term-limit text and any direct evidence of presidential support for or implementation of electoral and constitutional laws are not supplied.","The effect of irregularities on voter intent and the presidential result is unresolved; several allegations are disputed, preliminary, or not independently verified.","No opposition victory occurred, so acceptance of a verified opposition victory cannot be directly tested.","Conflict-related exclusion and descriptive underrepresentation do not by themselves establish a presidential decision causing those outcomes."] ,"corrections_made":["Added the omitted evidence on election-related violence, military-school polling allegations, women’s representation, post-election protest suppression, and the broader characterization of the election as highly contested.","Qualified the CENI register audit as an institutional, self-reported assessment rather than proof of presidentially independent administration.","Corrected the description of annulments to refer to annulled results or candidates rather than 81 annulled candidacies.","Preserved the distinction between formal competition and genuinely contestable power, and between institutional occurrence under Tshisekedi’s presidency and personal attribution."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if direct evidence is found on Tshisekedi’s instructions, oversight, remedies, or failure to remedy the documented electoral and protest-related defects.","Reopen if final judicial or observer findings determine whether the irregularities altered the presidential result or establish a verified opposition victory."]}
